DEN_Refugee
Zorru is one of the tiefling refugees seeking shelter at the Emerald Grove in Act One. Originally out on a scouting mission with  Yul, he encountered a githyanki patrol on the Risen Road before fleeing back to the grove.
“
We were s-scouting the road to Baldur's Gate. It saw us 'fore we saw it. Jammed its blade through Yul's belly, straight to the other side. And I just... I just ran.
„
— Zorru, on the githyanki patrol killing Yul

Description

Zorru has a strong survival instict, which may override other duties and obligations. As a result, he often chooses flight over fight, such as when he abandoned his fellow scout to die after they had been ambushed by a githyanki patrol. He values humor, especially in difficult times, and occasionally makes fatalistic jokes.[1]

He has grown to fear githyanki after watching one gut his friend.

Involvement

Act One

When  Nymessa and  Damays guard a captured  Lae'zel, they comment that Zorru was right to describe the gith as "Yellow as a toad, and twice as ugly" and that one of them killed his squad. Upon arrival at the Grove, if  Zaki sees Lae'zel, she comments Lae'zel is one of the toad-people Zorru saw. Either interaction may lead to Lae'zel insisting on finding and questioning Zorru about the gith he saw, with the hopes of finding their Crèche and curing the party of their tadpoles.

Zorru is in The Hollow, next to the storage hut. If Lae'zel is present, he questions her presence, and Lae'zel orders Zorru to bow. If the player character allows this to happen, approval is gained with Lae'zel and lost with  Shadowheart. If Zorru is not made to bow, Shadowheart gains approval instead, and Lae'zel gains disapproval.

The player character can question Zorru over the whereabouts of the Githyanki Crèche, which results in his giving information that updates the map with a marker. This advances ⁠Find the Githyanki Crèche.

When the party approach the Mountain Pass, they can encounter the corpse of  Yul, Zorru's friend and fellow scout. Using  Speak with Dead reveals that Zorru left Yul to die. If  Wyll is in the party, he calls Zorru a coward.

After defeating all three goblin leaders, Zorru leaves the Grove before most of the tiefling refugees, and travels to Baldur's Gate on his own.

Act Three

If he survives to Act Three, Zorru is with several other tieflings in the refugee camp near the Requisitioned Barn, within Rivington. His dialogue with  Cerys,  Bex, or  Danis reveals he miraculously made it to the city all on his own, but had some close calls with Absolutist cultists on the way there; nevertheless, he acquiesces that he did not have it as hard as the rest of the remaining refugees.[2]

Despite his own cowardice, he despises Zevlor for failing to act under pressure during the attack by Absolute Cultists.[3] Depending on the player character's conversation with him, he may change his point of view to understand Zevlor tried his best in an untenable situation.[4]

    "Zorru! You made it here all on your own?" - Cerys
    "It was touch and go. Some close calls - the cult have claimed every road between Baldur's Gate and Elturgard".
    "But from what you tell me, I had it easy compared to the rest of you." - Zorru
  3. ↑ Zorru: "Spare me your sanctimony. He died a failure, with the blood of the tieflings he should have protected on his hands."
